x: Well done to Gavin Mason (17), Marcel Fok (20), John Dawson (20) and Ian Wells (don't ask) who ran a pb split of 49.1. We were just pipped by Haringey in the sprint relay - not surprising as they fielded Mensah, Jarrett, Callender and Wariso.

A super finish from John Dawson in the 800m gave us just a glimpse of the power this Under 20 "Aussie" has beneath the bonnet. Unfortunately though, it was his last run for the Bels before disappearing off back home to Oz.

Darrell "Snakehead" Maynard had taken over and slithered around the course without dropping the baton before giving it to John "diarrhoea" Dawson who ran a storming leg in his rush to get to the toilet.

• Sadly we have said goodbye to John Dawson who recently returned to his native Australia. Still a Junior, John made a great contribution to our Southern League and National Junior League teams and even made a showing in the British League team at one point.

He started the afternoon off with a 2nd place leap while 400/800 man John Dawson kept anxiously looking out for jumper Kenny Pereira to show up before eventually having to fill in in this unaccustomed event.
Back from that horrible foot injury at Plymouth, John Dawson ran 1:58.8 on no training at all for nigh on a month - and then followed up with 200m and 400m relay stints.

It was nice to see Joe Nicholson back in action for the first time this season and he partnered Richard David to good points in the 400m while injury prone John Dawson turned on his normal blistering sprint to get up near the front in the 800.

Acknowledgements to Bob Bridges, John Dawson, Cynthia James, John Jeffery, Derek Jones, Bill Laws, Terry Lawton, Lionel Mann, Charlie Manning, Peter Matthews (NUTS), Pete Mulholland, John Powell and Jacqui Smiter for providing some of the results and team compositions.

As for the younger age-groups, there was a bumpy start for our team managed by John Dawson, with assistance from John Powell, in the McDonalds Young Athletes League, but they improved markedly and indeed won their last match; they did not qualify for the national finals but they have retained their…
All credit to John Dawson for taking over the Young Athletes' team at the beginning of 1998, hardly knowing what he was letting himself in for.

John Lambert will be joining John Dawson to share the load of managing the team and with Reg Hopkins gathering some under 13s around him to tackle Sportshall athletics during the winter, we should at least start off with some lads in this age group come next summer.
Without such support managing the YAL teams would be impossible. Thanks are also due to Reg Hopkins, Alan Mead, John Dawson and John Powell for their support throughout the season.

Tony supplied the team photograph that appears on page 9 of this magazine. Aussie John Dawson picked us up from Tokyo where he is now living and working. He ran with us while still a Junior in the mid-1990s.
